title: Hot Cross Buns
short: Traditional · C 4/4 · listen, then play it.
trouble: Reading notes one at a time instead of in chunks.

blocks.html: Three notes and three fingers. Put your right thumb on middle C, finger 2 on D and finger 3 on E, and leave them there the whole time. In bar 3 the notes go twice as fast: these are eighth notes, two to each beat.
What to notice: English nursery rhyme and street cry (the words were in print by 1767)

blocks.name: music-player
blocks.cap: Play it: the score scrolls, the keys light up, and “wait for me” lets you practise one hand at a time.

blocks.html: Play through it once with the right hand only, then add the left. Which chord change made you stop?

sources.name: Traditional tune, played in the three-note form that is usually taught first. Wikipedia notes that the rhyme is sung to more than one tune; no printed score was checked note by note for this one. Date of the words from Wikipedia.
